records.claim: Answered Brisson's incredulous questions about exotic travel with comic monosyllables ('Mon Dieu non!', 'Pas même le tour du monde!').

citations.quote: Pas même le tour du monde

records.claim: In 1904 forgot the title of Le Rayon vert, asked his wife, then laughed: 'One must be excused... if among so many titles the right one is not for the moment forthcoming.'

citations.quote: I really forget the name

records.claim: Had tried to trace all his heroes' journeys on a planisphere but gave up: 'Je ne m'y reconnaissais plus.'

citations.quote: Je ne m'y reconnaissais plus

records.claim: Denied 'in toto' that women play little part in his books (1894).

citations.quote: I deny that in toto

citations.quote: I am casting no disparagement on Mr. Wells

records.claim: In 1900 thanked a correspondent for a laudatory article: 'combien j'ai été emu'.

records.claim: Head drooped and voice saddened when speaking of not counting in French literature (Sherard 1893).

citations.quote: a ring of sadness sounded in the cheerful and hearty voice

records.claim: Memoir: tasting the 'sea' at low tide and finding it fresh — 'We have been hoaxed!' — then delight when the tide came in.

citations.quote: We have been hoaxed

records.claim: In 1904 'raising himself in his chair' to ask with animation whether Michel Strogoff was well presented.

citations.quote: Tell me, was it well presented

records.claim: Uses self-deprecating anecdote (balloon ascent that went only to Longueau; gendarme's hat; eight days in America because of a one-week ticket).

citations.quote: I had a ticket to go and come which was only good for a week
We sailed as far as Longeau

records.claim: Habitually turns to Honorine for confirmation ('we have read them all, have we not?'; asking her the forgotten title).

citations.quote: we have read them all, have we not

records.claim: Closes conversations by worrying he is tiring the visitor ('I fear that I am beginning to weary you').

citations.quote: I fear that I am beginning to weary you

records.claim: His French memoir is full of exclamations and rhetorical questions ('Timide ?… Oui, je l'étais'; 'Ah ! les délicieux loisirs').
records.caveats: Written, not spoken style; transcription cited only.

citations.quote: Timide ?… Oui, je l'étais
Ah, those delicious leisure hours

records.claim: Brisson: production as regular as his country's apple trees; Verne himself: provincial pride ('Je ne suis qu'un provincial, mais je connais bien ma province').

citations.quote: Je ne suis qu'un provincial

records.claim: He teased the caricaturist Baril about turning up as a solemn academician instead of his comic persona 'Gédéon'. He asked whether 'Gédéon' had caught 'phylloxera académique', and ended by asking him to bring 'Gédéon l'ancien' to future meetings.
records.caveats: Formal public speech (written to be read aloud as Director of the Académie): a performed persona, but in his own words.

citations.quote: attaqué du phylloxera aca
amener ici Gédéon l'ancien

records.topic: frank disagreement with a new member, announced humorously
records.claim: He announced that he would contradict Baril's praise of collecting, 'dussé-je être lapidé, à coup d'assiettes'. This explains the 'casseur d'assiettes' remark in his July 1875 letter to Heumbert (letter MJV B178), which refers to this speech.

citations.quote: dussé-je être lapidé, à coup d'assiettes, par les Potentiers de la ville

records.claim: To Dubois: 'Vous paraissez l'en blâmer; mais, contre vous, je pense qu'il eût bien fait'. He corrected the candidate on Paul-Louis Courier and praised him most for the passage that contradicted the candidate's own style.

citations.quote: mais, contre vous, je pense qu'il eût bien fait, cependant
J'avoue que ce passage est celui dont je suis le plus charmé

records.claim: He opened a compliment to a lawyer with a zoological parody of Creation: God giving the 'vertebrate, carnivorous, two-handed' being a glottis 'gave him more specially the faculty of becoming a lawyer'.

citations.quote: il lui donnait plus spécialement la faculté de devenir avocat

records.claim: He likes to turn a maxim inside out: 'On PARTAGE aisément les torts que l'on PARDONNE', and 'Quel plus gros livre... avec tout ce que l'on ne sait pas'.

citations.quote: On PARTAGE aisément les torts que l'on PARDONNE
avec tout ce que l'on ne sait pas

records.claim: In the year-2000 dream, doctors are paid only while their patients stay well (a 'Chinese custom'), Latin has been abolished after a candidate translated 'Patiens quia aeternus' as 'Patient parce qu'il éternue', and the narrator keeps bursting out laughing.

citations.quote: Nos clients ne nous paient d'honoraires que pendant qu'ils sont bien portants
Patient parce qu'il éternue
Ma foi, j'éclatai

records.claim: He opens by apologising for breaking with convention or for being an outsider, and redistributes thanks to others ('ce n'est pas uniquement au patronage du directeur actuel').

citations.quote: Voulez-vous me permettre de manquer à tous les devoirs d'un directeur
voulez-vous me permettre de les répartir dans une plus juste mesure
